basic_info.name: SiPhox Health (SiPhox, Inc.)
basic_info.category: At-home blood testing (hardware + mail-in lab panels) with AI interpretation layer — silicon photonics diagnostics startup
basic_info.stage: Growth-stage startup (founded 2020, Y Combinator S2020; 50,000+ members claimed 2026; home chip device still investigational)
basic_info.pricing_model: Wellness membership: $34/month monthly, $27/month semi-annual ($162 billed), $22/month annual ($264 billed); one-time purchase from ~$124; Ultimate 360 panel upgrade +$125 (up to ~59-62 biomarkers); GLP Monitoring panel +$75; free shipping; HSA/FSA eligible; cancel anytime. Home device marketed at $79/month on device page [uncertain: April 2026 press reportedly cited ~$99; not confirmed on site]. Historical: $95 one-off kits + $16/month (2023, TechCrunch). Free AI lab-test analyzer (Sai) launched June 2025 as no-cost entry point.
basic_info.target_user: Longevity/biohacker consumers, preventive-health optimizers, chronic-condition self-trackers (GLP-1 users, thyroid, cardiovascular), quantified-self wearable owners; B2B white-label for clinics/coaches
basic_info.scale_metrics: Funding: $27M total by mid-2023 ($10M seed co-led Khosla + YC; $17M Series A led by Intel Capital with Khosla, July 2023); LongeVC top-up March 2025; investors incl. Metaplanet, Alumni Ventures, Kortex, Duke Capital Partners, Bob Lee, Balaji Srinivasan, Paul Buchheit. Traction: 50,000+ members, 4.8/5 rating (site, 2026); ~30 employees (2023). Samsung Connected Care ecosystem partner at VivaTech June 2026 — durable threat signal (distribution via Samsung Health's 77M MAU). GetLatka est. $5M ARR flagged 'bootstrapped' — unreliable, contradicts VC record [uncertain]. Valuation undisclosed [uncertain].

product.core_features: 1) EasyDraw needle-free upper-arm blood collection kit (5 min, live 1:1 video support, same-day courier pickup); 2) 6 switchable panels — Longevity Essentials, Thyroid, Hormone, Heart & Metabolic, GLP Monitoring, Ultimate 360 (up to ~60 biomarkers across 9 categories); 3) results in 7-10 days from CLIA/CAP-accredited third-party labs; 4) unified dashboard: 7 health-system scores (Heart, Metabolic, Kidney, Liver, Thyroid, Nutritional, Body), BioAge, biomarker trends, future projections; 5) Sai AI chat (24/7) on results; 6) upload lab PDFs/photos from ANY provider (Quest, Labcorp etc.); 7) wearable integration (Apple Watch, Oura, Fitbit); 8) doctor sharing/export; 9) supplement recommendations + Care Action routines (morning stack etc.); 10) partner marketplace (Prenuvo MRI, gut test, 295-item allergy panel, 1:1 coaching); 11) B2B co-brand/white-label.
product.signature_differentiator: Silicon photonic chip that shrinks a benchtop immunoassay analyzer onto a semiconductor die ('shrink the lab onto a chip', inheriting multiplexing/sensitivity of lab instruments). SiPhox Home / SiPhox One countertop device: EasyDraw sample in, lab-quality results on the counter in ~60 minutes — investigational device, research use only, waitlist open (Aug 2026). Plus in-clinic variant (7 thyroid biomarkers in minutes, EHR sync, CPT billable). No competitor owns chip-level home immunoassay hardware + membership + AI stack; Samsung picked them as the 'diagnostic layer' of its Connected Care ecosystem (VivaTech, June 2026) — 'continuous device data + continuous biomarker data = complete health picture' (Dubrovsky).
product.lab_data_handling: Closed vertical loop: they ARE the lab order — membership ships EasyDraw kits monthly/quarterly/semi-annually (retest cadence chosen by user), processed at CLIA/CAP third-party labs (LDT regulations), 7-10 day results. Ingestion of external labs via PDF/photo upload of any provider's report into the same dashboard. Cadence philosophy: frequent retesting (monthly possible) vs annual blood draw. Hardware roadmap moves processing from mail-in lab to home chip (60-min results) and in-clinic point-of-care. No LIS integration, no FHIR surfaced.
product.family_dependents_depth: None found. Single-user accounts; no dependent profiles, caregiver mode, pediatric reference ranges, or hereditary-risk features anywhere on site, pricing, or press. Classic US solo-quantified-self blind spot — wide-open pillar.
product.doctor_sharing: Share results with doctor (doctor notified of new reports), one-click export, Sai generates 'doctor-ready summary'. No SOAP note, no structured consult brief, no doctor portal for consumer product. Separate practitioner motion instead: in-clinic thyroid device waitlist (retail revenue via CPT codes, EHR auto-capture) and white-label for clinics/coaches.
product.action_loop_monetization: Post-interpretation monetization is the membership itself: retest subscriptions, panel upgrades (Ultimate 360 +$125, GLP +$75), science-backed supplement recommendations, 1:1 coaching upsell, partner marketplace with member deals (Prenuvo whole-body MRI, Advanced Gut Health Test, 295 Food & Environmental Allergy Panel), 'Care Actions' daily routines (morning stack, wind-down) that create between-test engagement. B2B: co-branded/white-label Sai + panels for healthtech, clinics, physicians, coaches. No telemedicine/prescriptions observed; GLP-1 angle is monitoring (side effects/progress), not prescribing.

technology.ai_approach: Sai — LLM-based conversational analyzer over the unified profile (own labs + uploaded labs + wearables + goals), launched June 2025, free to start. Differentiator claimed: context + customization ('Why is my ApoB high if my LDL looks fine?'). Human-in-loop claimed: every report 'expert-reviewed'. No published model/eval methodology; classic LLM-wrapper risk profile [uncertain].
technology.data_inputs: Own EasyDraw blood panels (up to ~60 biomarkers); uploaded third-party lab reports (PDF/photo, any US provider); wearables (Apple Watch, Oura Ring, Fitbit — sleep/activity); user goals/questionnaires. Future: home device biomarker stream + Samsung Health ecosystem data.
technology.data_interoperability: Ingestion: PDF and photo/screenshot lab upload (strongest wedge — provider-agnostic), wearable sync. Exhaust: doctor share/export, EHR sync on the in-clinic device, Samsung Health SDK integration (June 2026). NOT found: FHIR, Apple Health Records, Health Connect, LIS/API public docs, WhatsApp.
technology.platform: Web app/dashboard (mobile-responsive, no native app surfaced), enterprise white-label offering; hardware: EasyDraw collector (shipping today), SiPhox One/Home countertop analyzer (investigational), in-clinic point-of-care unit (waitlist).

ux.onboarding: Two doors. Fast/free: upload an existing lab PDF to Sai → parsed dashboard + AI analysis in minutes (acquisition wedge, zero purchase). Paid: join → choose panel → kit ships in ~3 days → 5-min EasyDraw collection with live 1:1 support → same-day pickup → results 7-10 days. Time-to-value: minutes (analyzer) or ~10 days (first panel).
ux.data_visualization: System-level scores per organ axis (Heart/Metabolic/Kidney/Liver/Thyroid/Nutritional/Body), BioAge ('41, 4 yrs under'), per-biomarker reference-range tracking with visual progress indicators, trend-over-time comparisons between tests, 'future outlook' projections of what next test could show if plan followed.
ux.engagement_channel: Retention engineered around retest cadence (monthly option) + Sai 24/7 chat + daily Care Action routines (morning stack/wind-down) + wearable passive data keeping dashboard alive between blood draws. Channels: email + in-product AI. No community, no streaks proper, no WhatsApp. Transational-lab pattern partially broken by AI chat + routines — but core loop is still 'wait for next test'.

trust_gaps.clinical_validation_trust: Shipping product (mail-in): processed by CLIA/CAP-accredited third-party labs under LDT rules — credible baseline, but SiPhox itself is the interpretation layer on top. Claims: 4.8/5 across 50k+ members; 'pre-diabetes found in ~20% of tests' (2023, unreviewed); 'every report expert-reviewed'. Chip device: investigational/RUO; technical work published at SPIE (Mar 2024, 'At-home measurement of blood biomarkers on the SiPhox Home silicon photonics platform') and IEEE (2023), but no peer-reviewed accuracy-vs-analyzer correlation dataset surfaced on site [uncertain]. ZDNET (June 2026) fine-print risk piece on at-home tests includes the category. No clinical advisory board names surfaced on main pages [uncertain]. Risks: marketing biomarker counts drift (17 in 2023 → 'up to 60' 2026 across product lines); accuracy of the 60-min home claim publicly unverified.
trust_gaps.regulatory_posture: Home chip device explicitly labeled 'Investigational Device — research use only' + waitlist; FDA clearance pursued since 2023 ('within a year', TechCrunch) and still not obtained as of Aug 2026 — timeline slipped 3+ years, so the '60-min home lab' remains promise, not product. Mail-in panels ride CLIA/LDT regulatory lane (US FDA LDT-rule pendulum = structural risk). Sai AI positioned as wellness/education with disclaimers, expert-review claim as safety net. US-only distribution; no ANVISA/LGPD exposure (irrelevant in BR today, but the playbook — RUO device + LDT mail-in + wellness AI — is exactly the compliance ladder a BR entrant would face under RDC 657/2022).
trust_gaps.gaps_opportunities: Opportunities for Dr. Exame: (1) Zero family/dependents/caregiver/pediatric depth — the known US blind spot, Dr. Exame's pillar untouched; (2) no structured doctor workflow (SOAP/consult brief) on consumer side — only export/summary; (3) no community/WhatsApp-channel retention (BR retention face); (4) not in Brazil/Latin America, no Portuguese, no local lab integrations — the entire 'interpret the labs the patient ALREADY has from Dasa/Fleury/Sabin' space is open; (5) 7-10 day mail-in turnaround is the real product today — interpretation-first apps are not yet disintermediated; (6) AI methodology opaque — transparency (published validation, clear disclaimers) is a credibility wedge. Inspirations (not copies): free upload-any-PDF AI analyzer as top-of-funnel (proven June 2025 wedge); BioAge + organ-system scores as visualization contract; panel-switching inside one membership; GLP-1 monitoring panel (timely monetization); live 1:1 support during collection (kills the 'home collection fails' objection); Samsung-style ecosystem partnerships as distribution.
trust_gaps.relevance: High — the closest structural threat in this research set: owns collection hardware + lab volume + AI interpretation + action loop, and now Samsung distribution. BUT: home chip device still RUO (3 years of slipped timelines), mail-in results still take 7-10 days, US-only, no family layer, no doctor workflow, no BR presence. For Dr. Exame the durable lesson is the free universal lab-upload analyzer + retest membership; the chip is a 2027+ watch item, not a 2026 problem in Brazil.
